content.text:
Now I have a clear picture. The `New` entries are also ambiguous (common Go constructor pattern), so let me check if the graph is conflating those too.

Based on the graph analysis, and excluding common Go interface methods (`Len`, `Error`) that get inflated by name-based conflation:

h10.
`CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go` — approx 34 callers

This is a method on the filter `Engine` type (line 74) that compiles a filter string into a SQL statement. According to the knowledge graph, it has the highest genuine inbound-call count (~34) of any function/method declared under `internal/`. Its callers span the filter package's own tests and helpers, the `store/db/` layer (postgres, sqlite, mysql `ListMemoRelations`), and the server's API validation functions. Excluding it, the next highest are `NewEngine` (~32, `internal/filter/engine.go`) and `NewSchema` (~29, `internal/filter/schema.go`).

Note: The graph technically reports `Len` (`internal/version/version.go`) at 179 and `Error` (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`) at 142, but these are inflated artifacts — the graph conflates all calls to common Go interface method names (`sort.Interface.Len`, `error.Error`) onto a single definition. `SortVersion.Len` has only ~4 real callers.
